description: Per-page concept-id blocks for audit-inline-links.mjs --fix. When the audit would wrap a phrase on the named page with a link to the listed concept, the candidate is suppressed. Use this for cases where the matcher's contextless heuristic produces a wrong-target / inappropriate-level / awkward-position link that human review has rejected. Each entry should carry a short comment explaining why; the audit script reads only the page→ids map.

extremal-combinatorics.html.cf-roth: wrong Roth's theorem — extremal-combinatorics §X means Roth's 3-AP density theorem, but cf-roth is Roth's Diophantine approximation theorem (also Fields Medal, also 1955). Two different theorems by same person.

model-theory-basics.html.compactness: §X means the model-theoretic compactness theorem (consistency of theories), not point-set compactness (every cover has a finite subcover).

zfc-and-ordinals.html.compactness: §X 'Compactness, Löwenheim–Skolem, and completeness' is the model-theoretic compactness theorem, paired with logic-side companions.

variational-methods.html.compactness: §X splits the unit term 'concentration-compactness' (a single PDE method name) by wrapping only 'compactness'.

forcing-and-independence.html.completion-ca: §X 'Boolean completion of a poset' is the regular-open-sets / Stone-space construction, not I-adic completion.

etale-fundamental-group.html.completion-ca: §X 'profinite completion' of a topological/algebraic group is the inverse limit over finite-index quotients, not I-adic completion of a ring.

infinity-topoi.html.completion-ca: §X 'a different completion of set with topology' is metaphorical ('completion' as 'extension/refinement'), not I-adic completion.

partial-differential-equations.html.metric-spaces: §X 'gradient flows in metric spaces' is the Wasserstein / Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré program — metric measure spaces with synthetic curvature, not basic ε–δ metric spaces.

geometric-measure-theory.html.metric-spaces: §X 'Ambrosio–Kirchheim currents in metric spaces' is GMT-on-metric-measure-spaces (Cheeger differentiation), not basic ε–δ metric spaces.
geometric-measure-theory.html.compactness: §X 'compactness theorems for variant function classes (BD, GSBV, GBD)' is BV-style compactness in function spaces, not point-set compactness.

stochastic-processes-and-martingales.htm.cauchy-riemann: §X 'discrete harmonic functions on a graph' is the discrete-time martingale / random-walk notion; cauchy-riemann is the complex-analytic system $u_x=v_y, u_y=-v_x$ — wrong concept.

capstone-cohomology-story.html.open-sets: §3 uses 'topological spaces' loosely as 'manifolds-with-extra-data', not the formal point-set object
capstone-cohomology-story.html.cd-poincare-duality: wrapped 3× across §2/§3/§5 in PR #225; kept only the §2 introduction (hand-authored)
capstone-cohomology-story.html.hdg-applications: §5 'applications' is plain English (consequences/uses), not the high-dim-geometry topic

capstone-flt-story.html.completion-ca: §7 'completion' means finishing the Taniyama–Shimura–Weil proof, not I-adic completion

capstone-hodge-arc-story.html.hdg-applications: §2 'Applications' is inside a book title (Hodge's 'The Theory and Applications of Harmonic Integrals')
capstone-hodge-arc-story.html.compactness: §4 'compactness' is an everyday-precondition word in an active sentence about Hodge structures

capstone-langlands-arc-story.html.complex-numbers: §4 reader is parsing Satake parameters; doesn't need a complex-numbers primer
capstone-langlands-arc-story.html.holomorphic-function: §3 reader is already parsing newforms; doesn't need a holomorphic-function primer

capstone-local-global-story.html.completion-ca: lede + §2 + §5 + colophon mix metaphorical use ('completion gambit'), profinite completion (different construction), and redundant uses where 'completion' is already domain vocabulary
capstone-local-global-story.html.real-numbers: lede 'real numbers $\mathbb{R}$' is defined in the very next sentence

capstone-millennium-prizes-story.html.hodge-conjecture: §3 wraps the section opener 'The Hodge Conjecture' — awkward to link a section's title

capstone-sound-to-wavelets-story.html.hdg-applications: §6 'applications' is plain English in a list of practical use cases

cohomology-and-duality.html.chern-classes: §6 worked example (CP^n) is purely topological — $c_i \in H^{2i}(X;\mathbb{Z})$ via cup product. chern-classes (intersection-theory-chow, algebraic $A^i(X)$) is the wrong target; cc-chern-classes (topological) is correct.
